sources.title: The Probabilistic Relevance Framework: BM25 and Beyond
sources.venue: Foundations and Trends in Information Retrieval, 3(4):333-389

establishes.statement: Defines and surveys the BM25 ranking function used as BEIR's lexical baseline.
establishes.support_quote: (a) BM25 [55] is a commonly-used bag-of-words retrieval function based on token-matching between two high-dimensional sparse vectors with TF-IDF token weights.

sources.title: Bridging the lexical chasm: statistical approaches to answer-finding
sources.venue: Proceedings of the 23rd annual international ACM SIGIR conference

establishes.statement: Names the 'lexical gap' problem that motivates moving beyond pure bag-of-words matching.
establishes.support_quote: However, these approaches suffer from lexical gap [5] and are able to only retrieve documents containing keywords present within the query.

sources.title: BERT: Pre-training of deep bidirectional transformers for language understanding

establishes.statement: Introduces BERT, the pre-trained Transformer encoder underlying most neural retrievers evaluated in BEIR.
establishes.support_quote: Recently, deep learning and in particular pre-trained Transformer models like BERT [12] have become popular in information retrieval [37].

sources.title: MS MARCO: A Human Generated MAchine Reading COmprehension Dataset
sources.venue: unclear in source reference list (venue string garbled by extraction)

establishes.statement: Introduces MS MARCO, the large passage-ranking training set most BEIR-evaluated systems are trained on.
establishes.support_quote: Many prior work train neural retrieval systems on large datasets like ... MS MARCO [45] (533k training examples), which ... focus on passage retrieval given a question or short keyword-based query.

sources.title: Natural Questions: a Benchmark for Question Answering Research
sources.venue: Transactions of the Association for Computational Linguistics

establishes.statement: Introduces Natural Questions (NQ), one of BEIR's 18 zero-shot datasets and part of DPR's training data.
establishes.support_quote: Natural Questions [34] contains Google search queries and documents with paragraphs and answer spans within Wikipedia articles.

sources.title: MultiReQA: A Cross-Domain Evaluation for Retrieval Question Answering Models
sources.venue: not given in source reference list

establishes.statement: Prior cross-domain retrieval evaluation limited to sentence-level QA retrieval; 5/8 datasets Wikipedia-based, 6/8 with <100k candidate sentences.
establishes.support_quote: MultiReQA [19] consists of eight Question-Answering (QA) datasets and evaluates sentence-level answer retrieval given a question. It only tests a single task and five out of eight datasets are from Wikipedia.

sources.title: KILT: a Benchmark for Knowledge Intensive Language Tasks
sources.venue: not given in source reference list

establishes.statement: Prior broad evaluation of 5 knowledge-intensive tasks/11 datasets where retrieval is involved but not the primary task, and only from Wikipedia.
establishes.support_quote: KILT [50] consists of five knowledge-intensive tasks including a total of eleven datasets. The tasks involve retrieval, but it is not the primary task. Further, KILT retrieves documents only from Wikipedia.

sources.title: Dense Passage Retrieval for Open-Domain Question Answering

establishes.statement: Introduces DPR, a bi-encoder dense retriever trained with a BM25 hard negative and in-batch negatives; one of the 10 systems compared in BEIR.
establishes.support_quote: DPR [31] is a two-tower bi-encoder trained with a single BM25 hard negative and in-batch negatives.

sources.title: Approximate Nearest Neighbor Negative Contrastive Learning for Dense Text Retrieval
sources.venue: not given in source reference list

establishes.statement: Introduces ANCE, a bi-encoder trained with hard negatives from an updating approximate-nearest-neighbor index; also the source of the Hole@k metric used in BEIR's bias analysis.
establishes.support_quote: ANCE [73] is a bi-encoder constructing hard negatives from an Approximate Nearest Neighbor (ANN) index of the corpus, which in parallel updates to select hard negative training instances during fine-tuning of the model.

sources.title: Efficiently Teaching an Effective Dense Retriever with Balanced Topic Aware Sampling

establishes.statement: Introduces TAS-B, the best-generalizing dense retriever in BEIR's comparison, trained with Balanced Topic-Aware Sampling and dual cross-encoder/ColBERT supervision.
establishes.support_quote: TAS-B [23] is a bi-encoder trained with Balanced Topic Aware Sampling using dual supervision from a cross-encoder and a ColBERT model.

sources.title: Improving Efficient Neural Ranking Models with Cross-Architecture Knowledge Distillation
sources.venue: not given in source reference list

establishes.statement: Describes the cross-architecture knowledge-distillation training setup used for BEIR's BM25+CE re-ranker.
establishes.support_quote: The model was trained on MS MARCO using a knowledge distillation setup with an ensemble of three teacher models: BERT-base, BERT-large, and ALBERT-large models following the setup in Hofstatter et al. [24].

sources.title: MiniLM: Deep Self-Attention Distillation for Task-Agnostic Compression of Pre-Trained Transformers
sources.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems, volume 33

establishes.statement: Introduces the compressed MiniLM architecture used as BEIR's cross-encoder re-ranker (BM25+CE).
establishes.support_quote: We evaluated 14 different cross-attentional re-ranking models ... and found that a 6-layer, 384-h MiniLM [70] cross-encoder model offers the best performance on MS MARCO.

sources.title: Context-Aware Term Weighting For First Stage Passage Retrieval

establishes.statement: Introduces DeepCT, a learned term-weighting method combined with BM25; found in BEIR to generalize poorly despite strong in-domain performance.
establishes.support_quote: DeepCT [11] on the other hand used a BERT [13] model to learn relevant term weights in a document and generated a pseudo-document representation.

sources.title: SPARTA: Efficient Open-Domain Question Answering via Sparse Transformer Matching Retrieval

establishes.statement: Introduces SPARTA, which learns token-level contextualized representations and converts documents into an efficient inverted index; re-implemented for BEIR because the original code was unavailable.
establishes.support_quote: SPARTA [79] learned token-level contextualized representations with BERT and converted the document into an efficient inverse index.

sources.title: From doc2query to docTTTTTquery

establishes.statement: Setup replicated for BEIR's docT5query system, which generalizes well across BEIR datasets despite being lexical-retrieval-based.
establishes.support_quote: We replicate the setup of Nogueira and Lin [47] and generate 40 queries for each document and use BM25 with default Anserini parameters.

sources.title: TREC-COVID: Constructing a Pandemic Information Retrieval Test Collection

establishes.statement: Constructs the TREC-COVID test collection via pooling, the dataset used for BEIR's annotation-bias case study.
establishes.support_quote: TREC-COVID used a pooling method ... The annotation set was constructed by using the search results from the various systems participating in the challenge.

sources.title: Overview of the TREC 2004 Robust Retrieval Track
sources.venue: not given in source reference list (TREC track overview)

establishes.statement: Introduces Robust04, one of BEIR's two news-retrieval datasets.
establishes.support_quote: Robust04 [64] provides a robust dataset focusing on evaluating on poorly performing topics.

sources.title: On Biases in Information retrieval models and evaluation

establishes.statement: Names annotation/selection bias in retrieval evaluation as a general phenomenon; grounds BEIR's Section 6 framing.
establishes.support_quote: This is a source for selection bias [39]: A new retrieval system might retrieve vastly different results than the system used for the annotation.

sources.title: The Curious Incidence of Bias Corrections in the Pool

establishes.statement: Documents pooling methods used to reduce annotation bias in IR test collections, the same family of methods BEIR's TREC-COVID case study evaluates.
establishes.support_quote: TREC-COVID used a pooling method [38, 40] to reduce the impact of the aforementioned bias.

sources.title: A full-text learning to rank dataset for medical information retrieval

establishes.statement: Introduces NFCorpus, one of BEIR's three bio-medical-domain datasets.
establishes.support_quote: NFCorpus [7] contains natural language queries harvested from NutritionFacts (NF).

sources.title: An overview of the BIOASQ large-scale biomedical semantic indexing and question answering competition

establishes.statement: Introduces BioASQ, the largest bio-medical dataset in BEIR (~15M-document corpus) and pooled via lexical term-matching with boosting tags.
establishes.support_quote: For example, in BioASQ, candidates have been retrieved for annotation via term-matching with boosting tags [61].

sources.title: HotpotQA: A Dataset for Diverse, Explainable Multi-hop Question Answering

establishes.statement: Introduces HotpotQA, BEIR's multi-hop question-answering dataset.
establishes.support_quote: HotpotQA [76] contains multi-hop like questions which require reasoning over multiple paragraphs to find the correct answer.

sources.title: WWW'18 Open Challenge: Financial Opinion Mining and Question Answering
sources.venue: Companion Proceedings of the The Web Conference 2018 (WWW '18)

establishes.statement: Introduces FiQA-2018, BEIR's finance-domain question-answering dataset.
establishes.support_quote: FiQA-2018 [44] Task 2 consists of opinion-based question-answering.

sources.title: A Data Collection for Evaluating the Retrieval of Related Tweets to News Articles

establishes.statement: Introduces the Signal-1M(RT) related-tweets task, pooled predominantly via lexical term-matching techniques.
establishes.support_quote: Creation of Signal-1M (RT) involved retrieving tweets for a query with 7 out of these 8 techniques relying upon lexical term-matching signals [59].

sources.title: TREC 2019 News Track Overview

establishes.statement: Introduces TREC-NEWS, BEIR's background-linking news-retrieval dataset.
establishes.support_quote: TREC-NEWS [58] 2019 track involves background linking: Given a news headline, we retrieve relevant news articles that provide important context or background information.

sources.title: Retrieval of the Best Counterargument without Prior Topic Knowledge

establishes.statement: Introduces ArguAna, BEIR's best-counterargument retrieval dataset -- the one dataset in BEIR with long (average 192-word) queries.
establishes.support_quote: ArguAna Counterargs Corpus [67] involves the task of retrieval of the best counterargument to an argument.

sources.title: Overview of Touche 2020: Argument Retrieval
sources.venue: Working Notes Papers of the CLEF 2020 Evaluation Labs (CEUR Workshop Proceedings, vol. 2696)

establishes.statement: Introduces Touche-2020, the conversational argument-retrieval dataset on which BM25+CE, unusually, fails to beat BM25.
establishes.support_quote: Touche-2020 [6] Task 1 is a conversational argument retrieval task.

sources.title: CQADupStack: A benchmark data set for community question-answering research
sources.venue: Proceedings of the 20th Australasian Document Computing Symposium

establishes.statement: Introduces CQADupStack, BEIR's 12-subforum StackExchange duplicate-question dataset.
establishes.support_quote: CQADupStack [25] is a popular dataset for research in community question-answering (cQA).

sources.title: DBpedia-Entity V2: A Test Collection for Entity Search

establishes.statement: Introduces DBPedia-Entity, BEIR's entity-retrieval dataset, and is also the corpus used for BEIR's efficiency/latency measurements.
establishes.support_quote: DBPedia-Entity-v2 [21] is an established entity retrieval dataset.

sources.title: SPECTER: Document-level Representation Learning using Citation-informed Transformers

establishes.statement: Introduces the SCIDOCS evaluation suite; BEIR uses its direct-citation task for the citation-prediction retrieval task.
establishes.support_quote: SCIDOCS [9] contains a corpus T of 30K held-out pool of scientific papers. We consider the direct-citations (1 out of 7 tasks mentioned in the original paper) as the best suited task for retrieval evaluation in BEIR.

sources.title: FEVER: a Large-scale Dataset for Fact Extraction and VERification

establishes.statement: Introduces FEVER, BEIR's largest fact-checking dataset (Wikipedia-abstract corpus).
establishes.support_quote: FEVER [60] The Fact Extraction and VERification dataset is collected to facilitate the automatic fact checking.

sources.title: CLIMATE-FEVER: A Dataset for Verification of Real-World Climate Claims
sources.venue: not given in source reference list

establishes.statement: Introduces Climate-FEVER, sharing FEVER's Wikipedia corpus but with real-world climate claims as queries.
establishes.support_quote: Climate-FEVER [14] is a dataset for verification of real-world climate claims.

sources.title: Fact or Fiction: Verifying Scientific Claims

establishes.statement: Introduces SciFact, BEIR's scientific-claim fact-checking dataset.
establishes.support_quote: SciFact [68] verifies scientific claims using evidence from the research literature containing scientific paper abstracts.

sources.title: ColBERT: Efficient and Effective Passage Search via Contextualized Late Interaction over BERT

establishes.statement: Introduces ColBERT, the late-interaction architecture that is BEIR's second-best zero-shot generalizer.
establishes.support_quote: ColBERT [32] (Contextualized late interaction over BERT) computes multiple contextualized embeddings on a token level for queries and documents and uses an maximum-similarity function for retrieving relevant documents.

sources.title: Sentence-BERT: Sentence Embeddings using Siamese BERT-Networks

establishes.statement: Provides the Sentence-Transformers framework BEIR's software wraps for evaluation.
establishes.support_quote: It contains extensive wrappers to replicate experiments and evaluate models from well-known repositories including Sentence-Transformers [53] ...

sources.title: A theoretical analysis of NDCG ranking measures
sources.venue: Proceedings of the 26th annual conference on learning theory (COLT 2013)

establishes.statement: Gives the theoretical grounding for nDCG as an evaluation metric, cited by BEIR when choosing nDCG@10.
establishes.support_quote: We refer the reader to Wang et al. [71] for understanding the theoretical advantages of the metric.
